title: Robust Knowledge Distillation in Federated Learning: Counteracting Backdoor Attacks

C-a.quote: It consists of three core components: Automated Clustering, Model Selection, and a Knowledge Distillation Module. These components work together to detect and eliminate malicious influences while preserving the performance and integrity of the global model.
C-a.locator: §IV-A Framework Overview; each stage's purpose is stated separately and each is a defense purpose. Clustering: "This clustering process distinguishes benign updates, which form dense clusters due to their similarity, from potentially malicious updates, which appear as outliers because of their dissimilarity" (§IV). Model Selection: "This component refines the set of benign models by selecting the most representative ones for aggregation, thereby mitigating the impact of outliers and enhancing the robustness of the aggregated model against backdoor attacks" (§IV). Distillation: "To further refine this model and improve its resilience against subtle backdoor triggers in Non-IID settings, Knowledge Distillation (KD) is applied" and "Third, RKD ensures secure knowledge transfer by distilling from the carefully selected ensemble models, preventing the propagation of [malicious influence]" (§IV)

C-b.quote: Even after the clustering phase effectively isolates most malicious updates, some malicious or anomalous updates may still be present. Without employing the median to mitigate the influence of residual outliers, these outliers can disproportionately affect the aggregated model, resulting in unstable ASR measurements.
C-b.locator: §V-Ablation and §IV; the residual-coverage reason is completed at §IV, "most representative models, RKD further mitigates the influence of any remaining malicious updates. This selection forms a reliable and trustworthy ensemble for knowledge distillation." The deficiency of single-mechanism alternatives is stated at §II, "RFCL [1] employs HDBSCAN to cluster client updates for defending against gradient poisoning attacks, yet its effectiveness diminishes against adaptive backdoor attacks [22]. A critical limitation of these methods lies in th[eir]"

C-c.quote: Evaluation Metrics We utilized two key evaluation metrics: Main Task Accuracy (MTA) and Attack Success Rate (ASR).
C-c.locator: §V; the ASR definition is "ASR evaluates the effectiveness of the backdoor attack by measuring the proportion of poisoned inputs that the global model misclassifies into the attacker's target class", and the assembled framework's MTA/ASR are reported across CIFAR-10, EMNIST and Fashion-MNIST against DBA, A3FL and F3BA at 20-60% attacker ratios

C-d.quote: without clustering, RKD is unable to effectively identify and isolate malicious updates, allowing backdoor attacks to compromise the global model. RKD without Model Selection (Median). Excluding the model selection component while retaining HDBSCAN clustering, this variant effectively manages a 20% DBA attack ratio.
C-d.locator: §V Ablation Study ("Ablation study of RKD method against attacks"), whose arms are RKD without Clustering, RKD without Model Selection (retaining HDBSCAN clustering), and RKD without Clustering and Model Selection ("leaving only the knowledge distillation process"). coder_note:
AMENDMENT 3 RAISES A CODE HERE FOR THE THIRD TIME, AND THIS ONE IS THE CLEAREST OF THE THREE. The third stage is KNOWLEDGE DISTILLATION, which by the operation's name is a model-compression and knowledge-transfer device and nothing to do with poisoning. The paper anticipates exactly that reading and rejects it for its own predecessors: prior distillation work "focus[es] on improving model performance under data heterogeneity rather than explicitly defending against backdoor attacks ... To bridge this gap, we propose Robust Knowledge Di[stillation]" (§II). Its own KD stage is given a defense purpose in two places, quoted in the C-a locator. So the count reaches three defense stages on the paper's own words. C-a would reach YES on clustering and model selection alone, so the code does not DEPEND on the KD reading -- but the ablation does, because the arm that decides C-d leaves KD as the surviving downstream. Fedward, LASA and RKD are now three rows where Amendment 3 raises rather than lowers a code, and A5 must say so: the amendment was disclosed as being able only to lower the primary and DESIGN rates, and that disclosure is incomplete.

C-d = YES ON THE SAME SHAPE AS LASA, AND ON TWO INDEPENDENT ARMS. The pipeline is clustering -> model selection -> distillation. The "without Clustering" arm removes the most upstream stage while model selection and KD survive unmodified; the "without Model Selection" arm removes the middle while clustering upstream and KD downstream survive, and the paper states the retention explicitly ("while retaining HDBSCAN clustering"). Both hold a downstream mechanism fixed and vary what reaches it. This is not the DROPlet or CrowdGuard Table V shape, where the DOWNSTREAM component is the thing dropped; the rubric's leave-one-out exclusion therefore does not bite. The Q sweep in Fig. 11 is a second, independent route and would carry the code on its own.

C-b IS A THIRD DISTINCT KIND OF PAIRING REASON: RESIDUAL COVERAGE. BRFL's reason was cost complementarity, LASA's was matched threat complementarity, WFAgg's was adversarial complementarity; RKD's is that the upstream stage leaves a RESIDUE which the downstream stage exists to catch -- clustering isolates most malicious updates, some survive inside the benign cluster while still deviating from its central tendency, and the median-based selection removes those. C-b's frozen text admits it under "cover complementary threats or complementary regions of the attack space", reading the attack space as the region of updates that survive the first filter. Four kinds of pairing reason are now attested and the pre-registration anticipated two; A5 reports the taxonomy.

NOTE ON WHAT THE ABLATION SHOWS, BECAUSE IT CUTS TOWARD OUR ARGUMENT AND SHOULD NOT BE OVERSOLD. The arms are reported qualitatively in prose ("effectively manages a 20% DBA attack ratio", "performance is noticeably decreased") with the numbers in a table, and every arm is evaluated by the COMPOSED system's MTA/ASR. So the paper runs the identifying contrast and then reads it off the composed outcome, which is the correct procedure and is what Prop. prop:identification_full asks for. It is a C-d = YES and a well-executed one; it is not evidence for the paper's thesis that such contrasts are rare, and A5 should count it plainly.
